description:
The crate's integration suites build their repository from the shared taxonomy fixture, so no suite outside the library depends on the binary supplying a vocabulary.

## Background

The integration suites construct repositories the same way the in-module tests did, through the scaffold's default hierarchy template, and several assert on the type names it wrote. The fixture that replaces it is authored by the work this depends on; adopting it here is the same mechanical substitution over a different suite family, under a different build target.

The suites are enumerated rather than counted: the rules suites covering config loading, default-rule derivation, label-membership validation, schema regeneration and CLI warnings; the documents-and-templates suites covering template apply atomicity and the document event log; the derived-state repair suite; and the item-validation, query-graph and repository-workflow suites.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every integration test that asserts on a type name or a namespace builds its repository through the shared fixture.
- [hard] REQ-02: An integration test that needs only a repository, and asserts on no vocabulary, is left alone.
- [hard] REQ-03: No suite constructs the scaffold's hierarchy template to obtain a taxonomy.
- [hard] REQ-04: The suites pass unchanged, since nothing about the code under test changes.

## Notes

The fixture is consumed, not redefined; a suite needing a different vocabulary declares it beside its own assertions rather than adding a second fixture.
title: Adopt the taxonomy fixture in the crate's integration suites
